extraction.Name: not stated
extraction.Refused/Protested: patent was mailed to me on (unknown date)1918 and was accepted without protest as I took it for granted that it was issued in a legal way and had to be accepted
extraction.Recorded patent: It was filed for recording by me in Bennett County on the tenth day of March,1919,Book 1,Page 519,Bennett County,South Dakota
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Has not been sold but taken by mortgage foreclosure. The last mortgage was $5000.00
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: The land was mortgaged for funds to pay taxes and improvements on it. My first mortgage was for about $1100.00 and used to pay delinquent taxes and pay old mortgage and a few old debts and taxes. later, I had to give a second mortgage to the bank and later, made a new mortgage to pay off these former mortgages interest, taxes and other improvements. Mortgage was foreclosed and date of redemption has expired.
extraction.NOTES: State of Washington; patent stamped as received at the Pine Ridge Agency May 10, 1918 and mailed to allottee by the Agency; I never got a cent of this money but used it all for improving the land; all the money involved in these mortgages, except our bare living, was put on the land in necessary improvements; Fair health, sound mind, has no financial resources outside of his remaining interest in the Reservation and his daily labor; does not own his home; Wife and four daughters; 'I was not defrauded. The transactions were all apparently legal, though had the Government not forced me to take the deeds, I should still have my land.'
